items.title: What Silent Spring changed
items.claim: Rachel Carson's Silent Spring was published in 1962. Which US policy outcome is widely traced to its influence?

options.text: Founding of the US EPA in 1970 and the 1972 DDT ban

items.reveal_title: EPA founded 1970; DDT banned for agricultural use 1972
items.reveal:
Carson's book linked DDT and other synthetic pesticides to ecological damage. The chemical industry attacked the book; the EPA was nonetheless founded under Nixon in 1970.

DDT remains permitted under the Stockholm Convention for disease vector control.
items.why: Single works of science writing have sometimes redirected national environmental policy.

items.title: Living Planet Index decline
items.claim: The WWF/ZSL Living Planet Report 2022 reported the average size of monitored vertebrate populations had changed by how much since 1970?

options.text: Declined by an average of around 69%

items.reveal_title: An average 69% decline in monitored populations
items.reveal:
The LPI is a population-weighted average, sensitive to extreme declines in subsets. Critics (e.g. Leung et al., 2020) note skewed samples; the headline figure should be read alongside the methodology.

Freshwater populations showed the steepest declines.
items.why: Indicators that combine many populations can be both informative and easily misread.

items.title: Amazon dieback risk
items.claim: Research from the early 2020s suggests parts of the Amazon may be approaching a tipping point at what threshold of deforestation?
items.reveal:
Lovejoy and Nobre (2018) proposed a tipping point of 20-25% deforestation, combined with climate change, beyond which large parts of the Amazon could shift to savanna.

Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon stood near 17% by 2020 by INPE measurements.
items.why: Ecosystem tipping points have policy salience even when their exact value is uncertain.
